The two traces diverge significantly in their search strategies after deducing the same two core structural blocks. Trace 1 treats the problem as a block-fitting exercise, testing starting positions for the blocks and quickly homing in on the solution. Trace 2 begins with the same block-fitting approach and finds the solution, but then diverges by abandoning this line of reasoning in favor of a highly exhaustive, systematic enumeration of all possible mathematical overlaps between the two chains. 

This divergence results in Trace 2 executing a massive CYCLE of exploring and pruning numerous overlap configurations (Case 6, Case 10, Case 12, etc.) that Trace 1 never needs to consider. While Trace 2's exhaustive analysis eventually pays off by re-discovering the same solution via a different overlap case (Case 8), the sibling trace demonstrates that this entire branch was unnecessary, as the solution was already found and verified through the simpler block-fitting method.

Here are the annotations for each trace:

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's try to fit the blocks." end="So $i=1$ is impossible." basis="The solver opens a branch exploring $i=1$ and explicitly eliminates it, which directs the search to $i=2$."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's try $i=2$." end="This is consistent." basis="The solver opens a branch exploring $i=2$ and finds the valid solution arrangement."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Is it possible Palm is at 4?" end="So 1716 at 4 is correct." basis="The solver re-derives that $i=1$ is impossible, a conclusion already reached in the first CYCLE, adding no new information."

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's try to integrate the two chains." end="So $i \neq 3$." basis="The solver opens a branch exploring $i=3$ and explicitly eliminates it."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Case $i=1$:" end="So $i=1$ is impossible." basis="The solver explores $i=1$ and eliminates it after finding contradictions."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Case $i=2$:" end="This fits." basis="The solver explores $i=2$ and finds the solution, which pays off."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's check the overlap $s_1 = c+1$ again." end="So $s_1 \neq c+1$." basis="The solver re-explores the $s_1=c+1$ overlap branch and explicitly eliminates it."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's check Case 8 again. $s_3=c+1$" end="This configuration works!" basis="The solver reopens Case 8 and finds the valid solution, making this a paying branch."
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Wait, I assumed $s_1=c+1$ implies $s_2=c+2$." end="So Case 6 is robust." basis="The solver re-executes the logic for Case 6 to verify a pruned branch, adding no new information."
